chunks: Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) narrated in Qum in Rajab of the year 339 A.H. He said: Ali ibn Hashem informed me in what he wrote to the year 307 A.H. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd narrated to me from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Safwan ibn Yahya, who said: Al-Husayn ibn Qiama narrated to us, and he was one of the heads of the Waqafites. So we asked for permission for him to see Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him), and we did so.

When he stood before him, he asked him, 'Are you the Imam?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'I bear witness to God that you are not the Imam.' He said: So he looked down for a long time, head bowed, then raised his head to him and said to him, 'What is your knowledge that I am not the Imam?'
He said: 'Because we have narrated from Abi Abdullah (peace be upon him) that the Imam is not infertile, and you have reached this age and do not have a son.'
He said: So he bowed his head longer than the first time, then raised his head and said, 'I bear witness to God that the days and nights will not pass until God grants me a son.'
Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran said: So we counted the months from the time he said, and God granted him Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) in less than a year.

And this Al-Husayn ibn Qiama was standing while circumambulating, when Abul Hasan the first (peace be upon him) looked at him and said to him, 'What is wrong with you? May God confound you!' So he stood by him after the call.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَر: Abu Ja'far, referring to Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.), the son of Imam Ar-Ridha.
key_terms.الطَّوَاف: Circumambulation, the ritual walking around the Kaaba.
key_terms.الوَاقِفَة: A sect that stopped believing in the Imamate after a specific Imam, usually due to his death or occultation.
key_terms.عَقِيم: Infertile or childless; used here as a criterion for Imamate.

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ar-Ridha (a.s.) prove his Imamate to the Waqafites through the sign of progeny?
ai.summary: This hadith highlights the theological debate between the Waqafites, who halted their belief in the Imamate after Imam Musa al-Kadhim, and Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.). The Imam’s challenge regarding infertility was resolved by the birth of his son, Abu Ja'far, within a year, serving as a miraculous sign (ayah) validating his continued leadership. This event underscores the Shia scholarly view that divine promise and biological reality align to confirm the Imam's status.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-13 In the month of Rajab of the year 339 A.H. (950 A.D.) Hamza ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) in Qum narrated that Ali ibn Abraham ibn Hashem in the year 307 A.H. (918 A.D.) in a letter to me quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Obayd, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran and Safvan ibn Yahya, “Al-Husayn ibn Qiama, who was one of the heads of the Waqafites asked us to ask for an appointment for him with Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.). We made an appointment for him.

When he faced the Imam (a.s.), he asked, ‘Are you the Divine Leader?’ The Imam (a.s.) said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘I take God to bear witness that you are not the Divine Leader.’ The Imam (a.s.) looked down for a while. Then he (a.s.) raised his head up and asked, ‘How do you know that I am not the Divine Leader?’
Al-Husayn ibn Qiama said, ‘It has been narrated for us upon the authority of Abi Abdullah as-Sadiq (a.s.)that the Divine Leader is not infertile. You are old but do not have any children.’

The Imam (a.s.) looked down again for a while. This time it lasted longer than before. Then he (a.s.) raised his head up and said, ‘I take God to bear witness that in a while the Merciful God will grant me a son.’”
Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran added, “No more than one year after that passed and God granted Imam Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) Aba Ja’far (a.s.).”

The narrator added, “Al-Husayn ibn Qiama was amazed and standing somewhere while Imam Musa Al-Kadhim (a.s.) was circumambulating around the Kaaba. When Abul Hassan the first (a.s.) passed by him, the Imam (a.s.) asked him, ‘Why are you standing here? What is wrong with you? May the Sublime God surprise you!’ After this he became one of the Waqafites.”
